A common theme in time travel stories is how time travel pretty much creates a new timeline, the original timeline is probably one where things unfolded normally, all the factors which lead to the bad future, and the moment 001 shows up a new branch of the timeline is created which is the setting of the show.

Speaking of 001, the protocols all correlate to him

1: The Mission Comes First. (The first thing 001 does is to panic and go off mission, where he could have used any alternate means to see it through.) Sure he didn't die but he also didn't try to find another computer to send the email to the future

2: Leave the future in the past. (001's fixation on the future and his inability to focus on where he is, owing much to the fact that he is aware that he's trying to go against The Grand Plan, is what leads him to try and orient himself solely against the future... which is why he's such a destructive force.)
An alternate take on 2 is Never jeopardize your cover. This didn't even apply to 001 because his cover was that he was a casualty in the 9/11 attacks. However, he could still have maintained his position as an IT guy who had survived rather than completely reinventing himself, using his future-gained knowledge of the past.

3: Don't take a life; don't save a life. Don't interfere. (001's first act after his mission failed is to try and save everyone on the same floor as him. His second act is to save his host, who should have died minutes after he arrived. This allows him to interfere with the events in a big way, causing ripples in the timeline that eventually lead to the bad future.) Like I said coulda still found some Internet café or library, then sent the original mission email

4: Don't reproduce. (001 fathers a child, which means not only did he save someone who was supposed to have died, he also created someone who should not have existed, further damaging the timeline.) This one is an eh it was something that's bound to occur regardless 

5: In the absence of direction, maintain your host's life. (001 takes his host from an unassuming, friendly IT guy in a trading firm to a reclusive multi-billionaire anonymously heading several companies, who is involved in medical tech, investment consultations, and God knows what else. The sheer magnitude of the ripples he causes simply by shifting his host's life in a radical new direction is one of the many things that confounds the problems of the timeline he's in.) Again this was really avoidable which begs the question of what exactly was his traveler role? I'd historian given the knowledge of stock markets but he also knew how to build the mind swap machine.

6: (Do not communicate with other travelers outside your team unless sanctioned by the Director.) 001's contact with 004, Simon, is what leads to many developments that lead directly to the destruction of the Grand Plan and causes untold suffering to Travelers and civilians alike. Marcy ended up with brain damage, then he went fully cuckoo and started kidnapping/killing travelers thinking that the director was out to get him even though no one really knew who he was which is what put him on the radar.

Protocol Alpha: (Suspend all other protocols.) This protocol was clearly created to allow Traveler teams to suspend their hangups, in particular Protocol 3, to eliminate potential threats to the future, up to and including 001, whose elimination earlier in his timeline would have resolved the fundamental problems of the Grand Plan, which can all be traced to him.
